- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows (especially 1-3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or flat — model tends to push upward too aggressively.
- Underestimate late-period price peaks (especially 25-30 days ahead) when true outcomes show strong upward momentum — model fails to capture late-stage rally.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment (e.g., sudden price jumps) — model overreacts and peaks too high, then corrects downward.
- Mean-reversion bias in mid-term forecasts (10-20 days) — model often overcorrects from recent highs/lows, missing sustained trends.
- When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), model should not assume momentum — forecast should be anchored to recent mean, not extrapolated.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if last 3-5 days are volatile, don’t assume trend continues; use smoothing or lagged indicators for stability.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates final price surge — especially if true outcome shows late-stage breakout (e.g., >80.00).
